title: Pullback of concrete supported boundary products
statement: For any Cartesian square of closed supports, any tuple on the ambient scheme, and specified identifications of its zero scheme and its pulled-back zero scheme with those supports, the pullback of the transported concrete product equals the transported product of the pulled-back tuple.

source.place: Restriction, elementary invariance, and final descent paragraphs

proof.text: Induct over the ordered fold. The unit-normalized exchanges identify the empty product. Kummer naturality and localization boundary compatibility identify each principal boundary. The cup pullback law appends the next factor; the normalized positive tensor multiplication is the actual frameTensorNext. Uniqueness of support exchanges and monicity of the support immersion identify the specified support transports.

theorem frameProductOnSupport_pullback (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u})
    {Z X D Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ X) (j : D ⟶ Y)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] [IsClosedImmersion j] (q : Y ⟶ X) (t : D ⟶ Z)
    (sq : ChosenCartesianSquare t j i q) (a : X ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k))
    (c : ℕ) (f : Fin c → Γ(X, ⊤))
    (e : X.zeroLocusSubscheme (Set.range f) ≅ Z)
    (he : e.hom ≫ i = X.zeroLocusSubschemeι (Set.range f))
    (d : Y.zeroLocusSubscheme (Set.range (fun k ↦ q.appTop (f k))) ≅ D)
    (hd : d.hom ≫ j = Y.zeroLocusSubschemeι (Set.range (fun k ↦ q.appTop (f k)))) :
    P.functorialCupPullback true i j q t sq a (2 * (c : ℤ)) c
      (P.frameProductOnSupport i a c f e he) =
    P.frameProductOnSupport j (q ≫ a) c (fun k ↦ q.appTop (f k)) d hd
